content: PanoRef multi-origin coverage optimizer review and follow-up. A code review of the latest implementation head rates the algorithm architecture 8/10, search-mode correctness 7.5/10, and readiness for complex imported sets 4/10, concluding the math/search design is mostly right but blocked by implementation scale and one dangerous workflow decision. Strengths include a deterministic area-proportional surface sampler, origin evaluation combining occlusion, geometric normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility/usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality values, plus a genuinely joint pair mode that ranks all legal coarse pairs by bitset union before applying quality/contribution tie-breakers, within a shared coarse-to-fine engine (4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, separate fixed-first and joint branches). Blockers identified: (1) imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because every non-floor object stores its entire AABB as an obstacle and candidates within 0.3 m are rejected, so any origin inside a room-enclosing AABB gets zero clearance and is rejected—fix is actual geometry clearance (point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast) with per-mesh/cluster obstacle bounds and a regression test for one imported object containing a room floor, walls, and empty interior; (2) geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports because every triangle is expanded into JS objects/arrays/64-bit numbers (e.g., ~144 MB minimum packed for 3M triangles, several times larger in practice) and structured-cloned into the worker, with BVH recursively sorting JS index arrays and raycasts allocating temporary arrays causing GC pressure—fix is compact typed arrays (Float32Array positions, Uint32Array indices, optional normals, meshRanges, transforms) with transferable ArrayBuffers and a flat typed-array BVH, three-mesh-bvh, or per-mesh BVHs, avoiding expansion into three world-space vertex arrays per triangle; (3) geometry extraction still blocks the main thread because the panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene before creating/posting to the worker, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, and structured cloning can freeze the app before the worker reports progress—fix is moving extraction into the worker or chunking/yielding between meshes; (4) 'Apply to selected panorama pair' is conceptually wrong because the UI writes optimized origins directly into existing panorama references via updatePanoReference, but changing metadata does not transform the image from the new position and merely projects old pixels from the wrong point—correct workflow preserves existing panoramas and renders/imports new ones at the new origins (fixed-first: keep primary, move next capture to B, render new graybox, inpaint/generate styled panorama, import as secondary; joint: create two-origin capture plan, move to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, associate each result with its actual origin); (5) reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent because reachableCoverage uses the coarse sample bank and all coarse candidates while final combined coverage uses a different fine sample bank generated with seed+1, so the UI can show combined coverage > reachable upper bound (e.g., 83% vs 80%) and reachable captured 100%, and for fixed-first the reachable set is calculated before the arbitrary first origin is evaluated so the fixed first origin is not included in the reachable upper bound at all—fix is a common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency, and including the fixed origin in the reachable union for fixed-first; (6) fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation because rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position/distance, so an identical candidate position can survive—add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation; (7) the 'four-level refinement' is not truly iterative because all offsets are generated around the original seed (seed ± spacing/2, ± spacing/4, ± spacing/8, ± spacing/16) without selecting the best half-step result and centering the quarter-step search around that new result, so it is a useful multiresolution neighborhood sample but not the coordinate/pattern refinement described in the plan; (8) local candidates can float between floors because candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below the candidate and local offsets retain the original Y coordinate, so on sloped terrain or multilevel sets an offset can move over a lower floor while preserving the upper floor's camera height—fix is for each offset to find the floor under the new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance; (9) the optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules because the optimizer evaluates angle and texel density but the actual shader blends both panoramas only by distance when both are visible, so the optimized coverage result and visible result do not fully agree—fix is for the shader to use the same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. Testing assessment: current tests are good unit tests but the most dangerous cases are absent—(1) one large imported object containing an entire room, (2) a 100k+ triangle performance fixture, (3) reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant, (4) fixed-first candidate separation, (5) sloped and multilevel floors, (6) existing panorama origins remaining immutable, (7) candidate generation inside concave imported geometry—and there are no GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to the latest head, so the reported test suite has not been independently enforced in CI. Bottom line: the push is much better than the previous review, the two algorithms are truly implemented, and the joint search is not fake or merely greedy; the reviewer would preserve most of the high-level design and require the seven fixes above (replace AABB clearance with actual geometry clearance; replace object-heavy triangle/BVH data with typed arrays and transferable buffers; move extraction into the worker; remove the ability to relocate existing panorama references; recalculate reported metrics on one common sample bank; enforce separation in fixed-first mode; reproject local refinement candidates onto their floor), after which the optimizer would be a strong, credible feature, but right now it should work nicely on ordinary PanoRef primitive sets while the exact scenario motivating the feature—a complex imported production set—is where the current implementation is most likely to fail. Follow-up directive: rebase onto main and resolve the PR conflict; add an allowed-floor-region mechanism or at least robust imported-floor component filtering; run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add a full 100K+ optimizer integration test, not merely a BVH-construction test; set a goal to accomplish the above, and when work is complete, spawn a subagent whose job is to disprove that the goal is actually fully complete, have it report back what still is lacking, then fix that and repeat until the subagent is unable to find any holes in the implementation. Implementation actions taken: inspected src/engine/projectedStyleMaterials.ts and tests/multiOriginInteraction.test.ts; removed the stale PROJECTED_FALLOFF = 6.0 shader constant and replaced a dead test assertion guarding the old distance-only blend heuristic with assertions protecting the new optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominance modes (projectedQualityAt, projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0, projectedBlendMode == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0, and not.toContain('projectedConfidence')); ran the targeted regression test (tests/multiOriginInteraction.test.ts) which passed with 36 tests; ran the full unit test suite (42 test files, 371 tests passed, including projectionCoverage.test.ts with 10 tests running both complete optimizer modes on a 100k+ triangle indexed fixture, and WebGL pixel-readback tests for radial-depth occlusion cubemap, projected style compile gate, receiving projected-style material, and projected receive single-projector not blended 50/50 with rears falling back and modes differing); ran lint (tsc --noEmit) and build (vite build), both passing.
